listing_note: Euronext Amsterdam ordinary listing (AEX Index constituent), reports in EUR. Same underlying company as the US OTC ADR ADYEY (1 ADS = 1/100th of one ADYEN.AS ordinary share); this file is the EUR-denominated primary-listing version, updated ahead of the H1 2026 Shareholder Letter due 13 August 2026.
overview: Adyen is a Dutch financial technology company that operates a single, self-built global platform combining payment acquiring, processing, risk/fraud management, and (via its own EU, US, and UK banking licenses) embedded financial products such as issuing, business accounts, and capital. It serves large enterprises and fast-growing software platforms/marketplaces (customers include Uber, Spotify, Meta, McDonald's, eBay, Etsy, Starbucks, LVMH, and Lufthansa) across three commercial pillars: Digital (online-first enterprises), Unified Commerce (combined online and in-store retail/hospitality), and Platforms (embedded payments and financial products for SaaS/marketplace businesses). Adyen operates globally with EMEA as its largest region (~57% of FY2025 net revenue), followed by North America (~27%), APAC (~10%), and LATAM (~6%).

business_model.description: Adyen earns revenue primarily by taking a small percentage ("take rate") plus fixed fees on the total payment volume it processes for merchants, net of interchange and scheme fees passed through to card networks/issuing banks. Because it owns the full technology stack (gateway, processing, acquiring, risk engine) and its own banking licenses rather than stitching together third-party vendors, it can offer a single global integration with consistent performance, and is increasingly monetizing adjacent financial products (issuing, capital/lending, business accounts, money movement) on top of the core payments rail. Revenue is highly variable/transactional (tied to merchants' processed volume) rather than subscription-based, though the enterprise relationships themselves are extremely sticky (multi-year contracts, deep technical integration), producing recurring, compounding growth as existing customers expand usage ("land and expand"). More than 80% of net revenue growth historically comes from existing customers increasing wallet share, not new logo acquisition. Adyen pays no dividend and conducts no share buybacks — it retains 100% of profit to reinvest in the platform, so unlike most large-cap compounders there is no capital-return offset to dilution/opex growth, and equity-value CAGR is driven purely by earnings/multiple, not per-share count reduction.

revenue_streams.name: Digital
revenue_streams.description: Payments for online-first enterprises: subscription/media, travel, mobility, digital marketplaces, financial services
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~56% of FY2025 net revenue (€1,334.9mn, +9% YoY reported / ~13% CC); Q1 2026 €349.6mn, +9% reported/+13% CC — the slowest reported growth print of any pillar in company history, reflecting mix shift toward large, lower-take-rate content/subscription customers

revenue_streams.name: Unified Commerce
revenue_streams.description: Combined online and in-store payments for global retail, hospitality, food & beverage, entertainment, and travel/airlines merchants
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~32% of FY2025 net revenue (€765.4mn, +30% YoY reported); Q1 2026 €196.2mn, +24% reported/+28% CC

revenue_streams.name: Platforms
revenue_streams.description: Embedded payments and financial products (issuing, capital, business accounts) for SaaS platforms and marketplaces (e.g., eBay, Etsy, Lightspeed, Fresha)
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~11% of FY2025 net revenue (€263.8mn, +50% YoY reported); Q1 2026 €75.0mn, +35% reported/+40% CC — fastest-growing pillar and highest strategic priority given embedded-finance TAM

revenue_streams.name: Net interest income
revenue_streams.description: Interest earned on merchant float/settlement balances held at central and commercial banks
revenue_streams.approx_share: Small (~€12.6mn FY2025), sensitive to interest rate environment; management has flagged falling rates as a drag on net income growth even when EBITDA is strong

business_model.customer_type: Large enterprise (B2B) merchants and platform/marketplace businesses; skews toward large, complex, multi-region customers rather than SMB. Customer base includes Uber, Spotify, Meta, McDonald's, eBay, Etsy, Starbucks, LVMH, Lufthansa, Navan, iFood, Vietnam Airlines.
business_model.geographic_mix: EMEA ~57% of FY2025 net revenue, North America ~27%, APAC ~10%, LATAM ~6%. FY2025 processed volume €1,394.3bn (+8% reported YoY, ~21% ex. one large normalizing single-volume customer); Q1 2026 processed volume €382.0bn, +21% YoY.
business_model.balance_sheet_caveat: Adyen's reported cash balance (~€10.8bn as of recent filings) is overwhelmingly merchant settlement float held in transit as a licensed payment institution/bank, not discretionary shareholder capital. It should not be read as a 'war chest' available for buybacks, dividends, or large discretionary M&A — the July 2026 Talon.One/Orb deals (combined ~$1.2bn) were funded from available cash resources but represent a small fraction of the float-inflated balance sheet, not evidence of surplus capital generally being redeployed.

competitive_position.market_position: Tier-1 enterprise payments player alongside Stripe in the large-enterprise/complex-commerce segment; global market share remains modest (payment-management market share estimated in the high single digits, vs. roughly 25% for Stripe) given the massive, fragmented global payments TAM. Dominant position among large, complex, multi-channel merchants (retail, luxury, travel, marketplaces) that value a single global platform over point solutions; still building out share in North America and in the SMB/platform long tail, where Stripe is structurally stronger (developer-first, powers ~90% of the Dow and ~80% of the Nasdaq-100 by customer count, and is expanding upmarket with wins such as Microsoft and Nvidia). In 2025, Stripe processed ~$1.9tn in payment volume (+34% YoY) versus Adyen's €1.4tn (+8% reported/~21% ex. one large customer); Stripe's TPV growth has recently outpaced Adyen's, a genuine and worsening competitive datapoint rather than a stable status quo.

moat_factors.description: One codebase/platform spanning gateway, processing, acquiring and risk, avoiding the fragmented, multi-vendor architecture of legacy processors (Fiserv, FIS, Worldpay) and enabling faster feature rollout, more consistent uptime/performance, and unified data across channels — this is Adyen's core structural differentiator versus both legacy acquirers and Stripe's more modular, developer-first approach

Netherlands/EU credit institution, US Federal Foreign Branch, UK PRA/FCA licenses allow Adyen to run acquiring, issuing, accounts, and capital natively rather than through third-party bank partners, improving reliability, settlement speed, and margin capture — a regulatory barrier to entry few competitors replicate

moat_factors.factor: Unified Commerce (online + in-store on one platform)
moat_factors.description: Genuine differentiator most competitors cannot match at scale — combining online and in-store transaction data into one customer identity/recognition layer, evidenced by ~95% shopper recognition rate across channels during BFCM 2025 (837mn transactions, 99.9999% uptime). Legacy acquirers are typically online-only or in-store-only; Stripe is comparatively weaker in physical/omnichannel retail

Deep technical integration with large enterprise customers across multiple markets/entities makes migration costly and risky once embedded; churn among enterprise customers is reported at well under 1%

>80% of growth historically from existing customers increasing wallet share, not new-logo counts, reducing sales/marketing intensity relative to peers reliant on new-customer acquisition — the model is 'share of wallet', not customer-count growth

Proprietary real-time risk/conversion optimization layer built on trillions of transactions across the unified platform; a data advantage that compounds with scale but is still early and unproven as a durable pricing lever

weaknesses: Pricing power narrative increasingly disputed: Adyen revised elements of its pricing for large, high-volume enterprise merchants in mid-2026 as competitive intensity increased, and analysts (e.g., Berenberg) explicitly do not believe Adyen has full pricing power given its enterprise focus, expecting take rates to stabilize or slightly compress over time as mix shifts toward large, low-take-rate customers and financial-products cross-sell

Concentration in a small number of very large customers; loss or slowdown of a single large-volume customer (referenced repeatedly since Q3 2024) has materially distorted reported processed volume growth
Sub-scale in North America relative to incumbents (Fiserv, Global Payments/Worldpay, PayPal) and relative to Stripe's home-market dominance, despite ~27% of revenue coming from the region

Digital, the largest pillar (~56% of FY2025 revenue), has decelerated to its slowest-ever reported growth rate (+9% YoY in Q1 2026), raising questions about durability of the core enterprise-digital growth engine even as Unified Commerce and Platforms accelerate

History of two distinct large negative guidance/growth surprises (H1 2023 hiring-cycle miss; Feb 2026 guidance step-down) shows the model can wobble materially when investment/hiring outpaces revenue growth or when growth normalizes faster than the market has priced in

business.risk: Competitive intensity from Stripe, Checkout.com, PayPal/Braintree
business.description: Stripe processed ~$1.9tn in 2025 (+34% YoY) and continues to move upmarket into large enterprise (Microsoft, Nvidia), directly contesting Adyen's core segment; Checkout.com continues to compete for European online enterprise share; Adyen's own June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision is itself evidence of intensifying price competition

business.risk: Customer concentration / single large-volume customer distortion
business.description: A single large-volume customer (unnamed, referenced since Q3 2024) is normalizing/declining and materially skews reported processed volume and Digital pillar growth

Digital net revenue growth fell to +9% YoY reported (+13% CC) in Q1 2026, the slowest print in company history for the largest pillar; if this proves a structural mix-shift trend (toward large, lower-take-rate content/subscription customers) rather than transitory, it directly pressures the 20-22% FY2026 group growth guidance

North America growth has been volatile and partly driven by APAC-headquartered online retailers moving volume, raising questions about durability of underlying US enterprise wins versus Stripe's home-turf advantage

business.risk: Leadership transition across CEO, CFO, CPO and product simultaneously
business.description: Co-founder and Co-CEO Pieter van der Does has stepped back from day-to-day leadership for health reasons, leaving Ingo Uytdehaage as effectively sole operating Co-CEO; CFO Ethan Tandowsky departs effective August 31, 2026 (announced May 2026), with SVP Group Finance Hwa Tsao (joined Adyen 2025) named interim CFO effective September 1, 2026 while a permanent search continues; Gayathri Rajan was named Chief Product Officer effective July 1, 2026. This is an unusually elevated concentration of C-suite change for a founder-culture company, landing in the same window as the company's first-ever M&A integration and a step-down in growth guidance

financial.risk: Net income sensitivity to interest rates
financial.description: A meaningful share of net income comes from finance income on merchant float/cash balances; falling rates in the EU/US would compress this income stream, as flagged by management ("net income growth in 2025 was hindered by the interest rate environment")

A weaker US dollar was a specific headwind cited in FY2025 results (reported net revenue growth of 18% vs 21% constant-currency for the full year); large USD-denominated North American and APAC-billed revenue creates translation risk each period

Adyen closed its first-ever acquisitions — Talon.One (€750mn, loyalty/promotions platform, ~€60mn ARR growing 30-40% annually) and Orb ($335mn, enterprise billing platform) — on July 1, 2026, funded entirely from available cash. Co-CEO Uytdehaage is personally leading integration, concentrating further executive bandwidth risk during a period of parallel CFO/CPO transitions. This is a genuine break from 15+ years of build-not-buy discipline, and some observers read it as a signal that pure organic growth alone may no longer be sufficient to hit medium-term ambitions

regulatory.description: Operating as a licensed credit institution (De Nederlandsche Bank) plus US and UK licenses subjects Adyen to capital, AML/KYC, and prudential regulatory requirements across multiple jurisdictions; auditor PwC reaches maximum permitted term after the FY2026 audit, requiring a new auditor appointment for FY2027

regulatory.risk: Payments regulation and interchange/scheme fee changes
regulatory.description: Regulatory shifts around interchange caps, open banking, payment method mandates, and (in the EU) progress toward a digital euro pilot require ongoing compliance investment and could reshape merchant economics across regions

Expanding use of AI-driven risk/identity decisioning (Dynamic Identification, Adyen Uplift) raises exposure to evolving AI and data-privacy regulation (EU AI Act, GDPR) as these tools scale into agentic-commerce use cases

macro.description: Processed volume growth is tied to underlying consumer discretionary spending and e-commerce/retail volumes; management guided 2026 market volume growth to remain 'broadly in line with 2025 levels, reflecting continued macroeconomic uncertainty', and sell-side (Jefferies) has specifically flagged discretionary-spending softness risk into Q4 2026 given Adyen's exposure to postponable consumer purchases

US tariff policy changes have prompted some customers to reassess where/how they grow and pivot to new regions — a secular tailwind for Adyen's multi-market platform but also a sign of macro-driven volatility in customer volumes
Beyond the direct P&L impact on finance income, broader rate cuts could reduce net income growth even as core operating (EBITDA) performance remains strong

growth_drivers: Continued 'land and expand' with existing large enterprise customers (>80% of growth historically), especially cross-sell of Unified Commerce (in-store) to originally online-only merchants and vice versa

Platforms pillar acceleration — embedded payments and financial products (issuing, capital, accounts) for SaaS/marketplace businesses; Platforms net revenue +50% YoY in FY2025 (+35% reported/+40% CC in Q1 2026), issuing volumes +8x YoY reaching an 'inflection point', capital loan volume more than doubled with >80% repeat borrower rate

Intelligent Money Movement (IMM) — extending beyond payments into money-in/money-management/money-out for enterprises with complex fund flows (marketplaces, travel, mobility, insurance); CashOut reached a hundreds-of-millions-of-euros annualized run-rate while still in pilot

Dynamic Identification / Adyen Uplift AI layer — new intelligence layer improving conversion, reducing fraud/cost, and enabling new use cases (policy-abuse detection, personalized checkout, agentic-commerce readiness)
North America expansion — targeted hiring (550-650 net new hires planned in 2026, primarily US teams and global tech hubs) to close still-low single-digit US market share gap

Unified Commerce structural advantage — proven at peak scale (837mn transactions processed over BFCM 2025 weekend at 99.9999% uptime, 95% shopper recognition), driving continued wins in retail, hospitality, travel/airlines (LVMH, Starbucks, Lufthansa, Vietnam Airlines)

Emerging market build-out — India (new UPI integration, direct acquiring rails with Visa/Mastercard/Amex/RuPay), Japan, Brazil (Pix Recurring/Open Finance), Mexico; APAC leadership refresh (Gary Yang named APAC President effective Aug 1, 2026, succeeding retiring Warren Hayashi)

First-ever M&A: Talon.One (loyalty/promotions infrastructure) and Orb (enterprise billing) acquisitions closed July 1, 2026, extending Unified Commerce and Platforms into real-time decisioning, promotions, and flexible billing infrastructure for enterprise merchants

Agentic commerce positioning — early infrastructure build-out (with OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare, Visa, Mastercard, Agentic AI Foundation) to capture AI-agent-initiated transaction volume as a future channel

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 Shareholder Letter due 13 August 2026 before market open, with earnings call at 15:00 CET the same day — four days after this analysis was written
recent_developments.significance: Imminent binary catalyst; options market is pricing an unusually large move (30-day ATM implied volatility ~66%, near 52-week highs) and this print will be the first full read since the Feb 2026 guidance cut, the June pricing revision, and the CFO transition. Consensus expects H1 growth broadly similar to H2 2025 given management's own framing that Q1 is the seasonal low and H1/H2 2026 should be broadly similar in constant-currency growth

recent_developments.event: Gary Yang appointed APAC President effective August 1, 2026, succeeding retiring Warren Hayashi (retiring end of 2026)
recent_developments.significance: Routine regional leadership succession, but adds to the broader pattern of management-team turnover in 2026

recent_developments.event: Adyen closed its first-ever acquisitions — Talon.One (€750mn) and Orb ($335mn) — funded from available cash; simultaneously named Gayathri Rajan Chief Product Officer (effective immediately) and SVP Group Finance Hwa Tsao as interim CFO (effective Sept 1, 2026) ahead of Ethan Tandowsky's departure
recent_developments.significance: Consolidates the year's leadership transition into a single announcement: first-ever M&A plus a new CPO plus the interim CFO solution, with Co-CEO Uytdehaage personally leading integration

recent_developments.event: Adyen revised elements of its pricing for large, high-volume enterprise merchants as competitive intensity increased; multiple sell-side analysts (Berenberg, BNP Paribas/Exane) downgraded the stock in early June, citing pricing/take-rate risk for enterprise customers in Europe alongside broader growth-normalization concerns. Berenberg cut its price target to €1,095 (from €1,950) and moved to Hold from Buy; Exane BNP Paribas downgraded to Neutral from Outperform (~€890-1,450 target range reported across sources)
recent_developments.significance: First explicit evidence that Adyen itself is proactively adjusting large-merchant pricing in response to competition — directly relevant to the take-rate/pricing-power debate; the stock is down ~33-42% YTD (from ~€1,397 at start of January to the €800s-900s range in early August 2026) and ~72% from its August 2021 all-time high

recent_developments.event: CFO Ethan Tandowsky announced surprise resignation, effective August 31, 2026, to pursue an opportunity outside fintech; stock fell on the news
recent_developments.significance: Leadership transition risk; company reiterated no change to financial objectives; interim CFO solution (Hwa Tsao) announced in the July 1 update

recent_developments.event: Q1 2026 Business Update: net revenue €620.8mn, +16% YoY reported (+20% CC); Digital +9% reported/+13% CC (slowest pillar print in company history), Unified Commerce +24%/+28% CC, Platforms +35%/+40% CC; processed volume €382.0bn, +21% YoY; financial objectives (20-22% CC FY2026 growth, EBITDA margin broadly in line with 2025, capex up to 5% of net revenue) reaffirmed unchanged
recent_developments.significance: Growth reaccelerated on a constant-currency basis versus Q4 2025 and management characterized results as 'in line with our expectations', partially easing (but not eliminating) FY2025 guidance-cut concerns; Digital deceleration remains the key watch item

recent_developments.event: Adyen entered definitive agreement to acquire Talon.One for €750mn, expected to close H2 2026 (subsequently closed July 1, 2026)
recent_developments.significance: First acquisition announcement in company history

recent_developments.event: FY2025/H2 2025 results: H2 net revenue €1,270.7mn (+17% reported/+21% CC); H2 EBITDA €702.1mn, margin 55%; full-year net revenue €2,364.2mn (+18% reported/+21% CC), full-year EBITDA €1,245.7mn, margin 53%; take rate improved to 17.1bps in H2 2025 vs 16.2bps in H2 2024 on favorable customer mix; 2026 guidance issued at 20-22% CC net revenue growth (down from prior 'low-to-mid-20s' multi-year framing) and EBITDA margin 'broadly in line with 2025' rather than further expansion toward the (now-2028) 55%+ target
recent_developments.significance: Stock fell sharply (reported intraday declines as high as 17-20%) on the guidance disappointment, echoing (in a milder initial form, though the drawdown has since deepened through mid-2026) the August 2023 growth scare; this print began the ~33-42% YTD decline that continued through the June pricing-related downgrades

recent_developments.event: Investor Day 2025 held in Amsterdam; management reiterated ~20% medium-term annual net revenue growth ambition beyond 2026 and pushed/raised the EBITDA margin target to above 55% by 2028 (from the original 2026 target set at the 2023 Investor Day); committed to providing formal annual net revenue guidance at the start of each year going forward
recent_developments.significance: New, more transparent guidance cadence, but the margin target push-out (2026 → 2028) is viewed by some analysts as a signal of continued elevated investment needs and structurally lower near-term operating leverage than originally promised

guidance.as_of: Q1 2026 Business Update (May 2026); H1 2026 Shareholder Letter due 13 August 2026 will be the next update

items.target: 20-22% YoY on a constant currency basis
items.vs_prior: lowered vs. prior 'low-to-mid-twenties' multi-year ambition set at the Nov 2023 Investor Day; unchanged/reaffirmed since the Feb 2026 cut, including at the May 2026 Q1 update
items.notes: Management has stated Q1 is the seasonally lowest-growth quarter, with H1 and H2 2026 expected to be broadly similar in constant-currency growth; market (industry) volume growth expected broadly in line with 2025 levels amid macro uncertainty. This is the guidance the 13 August H1 2026 letter will be tested against

items.vs_prior: target pushed out from the original 2026 target (set at Nov 2023 Investor Day) to 2028 (reaffirmed at Nov 2025 Investor Day)
items.notes: 2026 EBITDA margin expected to remain 'broadly in line with 2025' (~53% FY, though H2 2025 alone was already 55%) rather than expand further, as Adyen continues to invest in product/infrastructure and hiring
Majority of capex relates to data centers supporting growth; FY2025 actual capex was 5% of net revenue (€116.8mn)

items.vs_prior: consistent pace with 2025 (426 net new FTEs in FY2025); 88 net new FTEs added in Q1 2026, primarily commercial/tech roles outside Amsterdam
items.notes: Primarily across U.S. commercial teams and global tech hubs; headcount expected to evolve 'in a measured way'

Sell-side skepticism has grown since the June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision and downgrades; some models (e.g., Loop Capital previously) see 17-19% by 2028 as more realistic without further take-rate or market-share assumptions

guidance.management_commentary: At the Q1 2026 update management (Co-CEO Ingo Uytdehaage, then-CFO Ethan Tandowsky) described results as 'in line with our expectations' and reiterated all financial objectives unchanged. Management has continued to frame 2026 as a year of deliberate reinvestment (product/infrastructure, Dynamic Identification, Unified Commerce, financial products, US hiring, and now Talon.One/Orb integration) rather than near-term margin expansion, while maintaining the longer-term ~20% growth / 55%+ EBITDA margin (by 2028) targets. The June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision was not accompanied by a change to formal guidance, but sell-side analysts have interpreted it as evidence that maintaining current take rates against competitive pressure requires active management action rather than being a passive given. The 13 August 2026 H1 Shareholder Letter is the first full update since that pricing revision and since the CFO/CPO leadership changes, and will be a key test of whether 20-22% FY2026 growth and 'broadly in line with 2025' EBITDA margin guidance holds.

bull_case: Best-in-class enterprise payments platform with a structural technology (single global stack) and banking-license moat that legacy, fragmented competitors (Fiserv, FIS, Worldpay) cannot easily replicate, evidenced by 53-55% EBITDA margins and mid-teens-to-20%+ revenue growth even as guidance normalizes

Platforms and embedded financial products (issuing, capital, IMM) are inflecting (issuing volumes +8x YoY, capital loans doubling, Platforms +35-50% YoY) and represent a large incremental TAM on top of the core payments business, extending the growth runway well beyond simple volume-based take-rate economics

Severe cumulative share-price reset (down ~33-42% YTD in 2026 and ~72% from the August 2021 all-time high) may offer an attractive entry point if the 20-22% FY2026 guidance and take-rate stability prove conservative, echoing the pattern after the 2023 growth scare when the stock re-rated sharply higher once 2024 results reaccelerated

Land-and-expand model with >80% of growth from existing blue-chip enterprise customers and sub-1% enterprise churn provides high revenue visibility and low customer-acquisition cost relative to peers reliant on new-logo growth

Unified Commerce data/recognition advantage (95% shopper recognition at BFCM peak) and the emerging Dynamic Identification/AI layer create a widening data-driven moat as more transaction volume, including new Talon.One/Orb capabilities, flows through the single platform
bear_case: Digital, the company's largest pillar (~56% of revenue), has decelerated to its slowest-ever reported growth (+9% YoY in Q1 2026); combined with the June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision, this is direct evidence that take-rate/pricing power is under genuine pressure from mix shift and competition (Stripe, Checkout.com), not just a market narrative

Three distinct negative catalysts have compounded within roughly six months (Feb 2026 guidance cut, May 2026 CFO resignation, June 2026 pricing revision/analyst downgrades), driving the stock down ~72% from its 2021 peak — a magnitude of drawdown that raises the question of whether the market is now correctly pricing structurally lower growth/margin trajectory rather than merely overreacting

Leadership transition risk is unusually broad for a founder-culture company at a single point in time: Co-CEO/co-founder Pieter van der Does has stepped back for health reasons, CFO Ethan Tandowsky departed effective August 2026 (interim replacement named), and a new Chief Product Officer started July 2026 — concentrated turnover across the C-suite during the company's first-ever M&A integration

First-ever M&A (Talon.One, Orb, combined ~$1.2bn) breaks with 15+ years of Adyen's disciplined build-not-buy culture, introducing integration risk led personally by the Co-CEO and raising the question of whether organic growth alone has become insufficient to hit medium-term targets

EBITDA margin target of 55%+ has already been pushed out once (from 2026 to 2028), 2026 margin is guided flat versus 2025, and net income remains exposed to falling interest income as rates decline — implying limited near-term earnings leverage even if top-line growth holds at 20-22%
key_metrics_to_watch: H1 2026 net revenue growth on a constant-currency basis (due 13 Aug 2026) vs. 20-22% FY2026 guidance, and whether H1/H2 growth is confirmed 'broadly similar' as management indicated
Take rate (bps) following the June 2026 large-merchant pricing revision — must hold near/above ~16.5-17bps to validate the pricing-power thesis
Digital pillar growth specifically — whether the Q1 2026 deceleration to +9% reported/+13% CC persists or reaccelerates
EBITDA margin trajectory toward the 55%+ by 2028 target (H2 2025 already printed 55%; watch for H1 2026 seasonality)
Processed volume growth excluding the single large-volume customer distortion
Platforms pillar net revenue growth and financial products (issuing volume, capital loan volume, IMM/CashOut run-rate) as a proxy for embedded-finance monetization
North America net revenue growth and market share progress relative to Stripe
Permanent CFO appointment (beyond interim Hwa Tsao, effective Sept 1, 2026) and any further management board changes
Talon.One/Orb integration progress and contribution to Unified Commerce/Platforms cross-sell
Free cash flow conversion ratio (86% in H2 2025) and capex as % of net revenue (target: up to 5%)
Sell-side rating/price-target trend following the H1 2026 print — whether the June 2026 downgrade wave (Berenberg, BNP Paribas/Exane) extends or reverses
